findings.title: The till line names no tills and nothing compares Shelfmark with the owner's current routine

location.description: the "Works with your till" fact line and the page as a whole

findings.viewer_experience: An owner whose till or card reader is not named assumes it is not supported, and nothing tells them how Shelfmark beats walking the shelves on Monday or reading the till's own sales report.

current.value: The till line names no tills or card readers, and the page has no comparison with the owner's current routine

findings.target: The till line names the supported tills or card readers, and one line compares Shelfmark with the owner's current routine.
findings.fix_direction: The maker names the supported tills or card readers, and adds one line that compares Shelfmark with the owner's current routine. The maker must supply both facts; do not invent them.

closed_when.check: In the desktop, phone, tablet and widescreen viewports, the "Works with your till" line names the supported tills or card readers, and one line compares Shelfmark with the owner's current routine.

findings.title: Nothing follows up the Pricing and "Shops using it" nav links

location.description: the empty area below the fact lines

findings.viewer_experience: The bottom third of the desktop screen is blank, and a visitor who wonders about price or about other shops has to click away to find out.

current.value: content ends at about y=537 of 800 on desktop, with nothing below it

findings.target: A short pricing and shops section below the fact lines answers the Pricing and "Shops using it" links.
findings.fix_direction: Add a short pricing and shops section below the fact lines. The maker must supply the pricing and shop facts; do not invent them.

closed_when.check: In the desktop and widescreen viewports, a pricing and shops section sits below the fact lines and the bottom of the screen is no longer blank.

findings.title: Type sizes 16 and 14 px are only 2 px apart

location.description: the table and date text at 14 px next to the 16 px body text

findings.viewer_experience: The two body-level sizes look almost the same, so they do not read as two clear levels.
findings.target: The two levels read as clearly different: the table and date text at 13 px, or at 16 px set apart by color.
findings.fix_direction: Keep 16 px for body. Either take the table and date text down to 13 px, or put it at 16 px and set it apart by color.

closed_when.check: type_sizes in the desktop, phone, tablet and widescreen viewports no longer holds two sizes within 2 px of each other

findings.title: Tablet fact lines run too wide and leave short last lines

location.description: the second fact line on tablet

findings.viewer_experience: The second line runs 76 characters across 600 px, and "they happen." and "they take." sit as short last lines.
findings.target: Fact lines about 34em wide on tablet.
findings.fix_direction: Cap the width of the fact lines at about 34em on tablet.

closed_when.check: characters_per_line of section.facts > p:nth-of-type(2) in the tablet viewport is under 75, and no fact line ends in a short last line

findings.title: Two table titles wrap to two lines on the phone

location.description: the Title column cells "Notes from the Ferry" and "The Glass Orchard" in the phone table

findings.viewer_experience: Two of the five rows are twice as tall as the others, so the table looks uneven.
findings.target: Each title in the Title column fits on one line.
findings.fix_direction: Give the Title column more width, for example by shortening "Sold this week" to "Sold" with the week shown in the table heading.

closed_when.check: lines of tbody > tr:nth-of-type(4) > td:nth-of-type(1) and tbody > tr:nth-of-type(5) > td:nth-of-type(1) in the phone viewport is 1
